decisions.executionNote: Begin gradual elbow-up approach, orienting both open grippers downward within their own workspaces; piece positions and peg mapping will be checked visually.
Approach the left blue block and inner right purple star from above, completing downward orientation. Maintain separated arms and inspect wrist alignment before descent.
Use smaller increments after the right-arm continuity stop. Descend over the blue block and star, then close both grippers; retention remains unverified.
Lift closed grippers to check retention, then transfer the blue block above the leftmost peg and star above the third peg, leaving vertical clearance.
Blue is visibly retained; refine its alignment and lower cautiously toward the tallest peg. The star is not visibly retained, so open and clear the right gripper for inspection.
Peg tip is visible through blue hole; lower onto the base and release, then withdraw. Reposition the right gripper over the displaced inner star for a closer visual grasp check.
First blue appears seated around its peg. Clear it and approach the nearby yellow square. Correct the star approach using wrist-image offset, keeping grippers open until centered.
Center the yellow square and star using wrist views, descend to grasp height, close fully, and make a short test lift to verify retention.
Star appears retained; lift and carry it toward its peg, compensating for its off-center grasp. Yellow was not retained, so reopen and yaw to grasp its sides rather than corners.
Tracking interruption coincided with the wrists approaching each other. Replan from measured poses: withdraw the left arm laterally, then advance the visibly retained star with the right arm only.
Previous command executed zero steps. Use a minimal right-arm continuity correction and smaller leftward withdrawal to separate the wrists without further approach.
Correct the rejected tensor; no previous motion occurred. Withdraw left arm and descend the open right gripper over the star, then close for a retention test.
The star is grasped near its lower tips, not its center. Reopen, correct the close-range wrist offset, and test-lift. Approach the yellow square with the left gripper still open.
Star appears retained after lift. Carry it above the third peg with clearance. Center and lower the left gripper around the yellow square, close, then test-lift.
Both pieces appear retained. Keep the yellow clear while correcting the star hole over its peg and lowering slowly for insertion; inspect before release.
Star appears offset and tilted on the peg edge. Lift slightly, shift its hole left/back toward the peg, and retry a shallow insertion while retaining the yellow.
Peg is visible inside the star hole. Finish the shallow descent, release, then lift and clear the right wrist; hold the yellow until the adjacent peg is accessible.
Star is perched rather than seated; leave it for a corrective regrasp. Clear the right arm and bring the retained yellow over its peg, accounting for the grasp offset.
Lower the yellow slowly while its peg is visible in the hole, retaining it until seating is checked. Move the open right arm toward the outer star with clearance.
Yellow has not seated; lift it clear, correct its hole toward the visible peg, and approach again. Center the outer star using its wrist-view lateral offset before descending.
Refine yellow alignment by a few millimeters, lower and release. Center the outer star between the fingers, close at grasp height, and test-lift without assuming retention.
Yellow remains perched with the peg off-center in its hole. Regrasp, lift clear, shift slightly toward the visible peg, and lower again. Keep the retained outer star stationary.
Withdraw the open left gripper to inspect the yellow without occlusion. Bring the retained outer star inward above the board while keeping the wrists separated.
Use the star's observed displacement between views to compensate its grasp offset. Lift and align over the star peg, keeping clear of the perched piece; withdraw the left arm.
The first star now shows its peg through the hole. Lower the retained star along the aligned vertical path while approaching the red ring with the open left gripper.
Wrist view shows the carried star still forward of the seated star; lift and correct its lateral alignment before further insertion. Center, close, and test-lift the red ring with the left arm.
Recenter the carried star over the peg in the calibrated head view, descend, and release for an unobstructed seating check. Lift and withdraw the retained red ring on the left.
Clear the right wrist to inspect the released stars. Move the retained red ring to a central table handoff area, keeping the left EE on its own side and the arms separated.
Tracking stopped near adjacent wrists. Replan from observed poses and separate the arms first, retaining the ring and clearing the open right gripper away from the board.
Place the red ring on the central front table for a sequential handoff, without crossing the left EE into the right workspace. Right arm stays clear until left withdraws.
Red is released on the table. Withdraw the left arm well clear before bringing the open right gripper toward the handoff location.
Approach the central ring with the right gripper while keeping its EE on the right side. Move the left arm toward the outer yellow piece, staying in the left workspace.
Correct the ring's near-side offset and tilt the right gripper slightly inward without crossing its EE over center; close and test-lift. Descend the left gripper above the outer yellow.
Ring was not retained; reopen and lower farther at its updated location, using inward tilt while keeping right EE positive. Make a small left-wrist alignment correction before closing on yellow.
Correct the rejected tensor from the unchanged observation. Increase inward wrist tilt for the ring, then close and test-lift. Lift and recenter the open left gripper over yellow before descending.
Retry the ring lower with a small lateral correction, then test retention. Recenter the left gripper over yellow at clearance before descending, using the observed wrist-image response.
Yellow is centered between the open fingers; close and lift to verify retention. Retry the ring at a shallower height to avoid pushing it along the table, then test-lift.
Neither piece was retained. Reopen and correct the yellow's lateral offset; retry both at a lower grasp plane with a short closed-gripper lift to verify retention.
Both objects remain on the table, below the finger contact region. Reopen, shift the grasp centers toward the near sides, and retry a short lift rather than transferring unverified grasps.
Change the unsuccessful approach: rotate the open left gripper to grasp square edges rather than corners. Clear the right arm and remove its excessive inward tilt before another ring strategy.
Square edges now align with the left jaws. Correct its lateral offset, descend, and test-lift. Approach the remaining right-side yellow with the open right gripper while leaving the ring undisturbed.
Align both grippers with the square side faces rather than corners, correct the displaced left square center, descend to grasp height, and close before checking retention.
Both square pieces appear between the jaws. Lift with closed grippers to verify retention, then bring the left square inward while the right remains well separated.
Both squares remain visibly retained. Transfer the left square toward its peg at clearance height; keep the right square stationary until the placement area is clear.
Align the retained left square's hole with the second peg using its observed translation in the head image, then make a shallow descent. Keep the third square held clear on the right.
Placement is obstructed by the tilted first square. Withdraw the retained left square and set the right square down in a clear right-side staging area, freeing the right arm for correction.

The obstructing square has moved off the peg. Use the carried square's measured image displacement to compensate its grasp offset, align over the now-clear peg, and descend cautiously while the right wrist withdraws.
The held yellow is centered over the peg in the head view. Make a slow vertical insertion while keeping it closed for inspection; move the empty right wrist away from the board.
The yellow peg is now visible within the hole. Make a millimeter-scale centering correction, finish the descent, release, and withdraw for a clear seating check.
Withdraw from the released square without disturbing it. Approach the red ring with the left arm for a better-centered pickup and a controlled handoff; keep the right arm clear.
Simplify the ring approach by returning the open left gripper toward a world-aligned downward orientation while centering above it. Keep the right arm stationary and clear.
Center the ring between the left jaws, descend to pickup height, close, and test-lift before attempting another transfer.
The ring remained on the table and the jaws contacted only its far rim. Reopen, shift the grasp nearer its center, lower slightly, and test retention again.
Retention is still uncertain. Make a modest lift and lateral test with the left gripper closed; compare the ring's motion against the table before planning a transfer.
Ring is not retained. Reapproach open, shifting the wrist farther toward the near side so the ring center enters the finger contact region rather than only its rim, then close.
The ring is now centered across the jaws. Lift to verify retention, then bring it toward a central handoff with a slight outward tool tilt while keeping the left EE on its own side.
Ring retention is now visible. Lower it into the central-right handoff area, release gently, and begin withdrawing the left arm before the right approaches.
Withdraw the left arm and approach the newly staged ring with the right gripper, gradually restoring a simple downward orientation. Keep both open and separated.
Use the newly staged ring's position and the gripper-to-link offset to center the right jaws, descend, close, and test-lift. Left arm remains withdrawn.
Ring is visibly retained after lifting. Raise it clear of the pieces and transfer above the shortest, rightmost peg, compensating the forward gripper offset.
Lower the retained ring vertically toward the shortest peg in small increments, keeping the current lateral alignment and checking the hole before releasing.
The peg remains behind the ring rather than centered. Lift for clearance, compensate the gripper-to-link forward offset, and approach the peg again without releasing.
With the ring repositioned over the shortest peg, continue a slow vertical descent and pause to inspect insertion before release.
